assembly tooling constructed by the University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC)

sensors on opposite sides of a module, the assembly was performed separately for the two sides. From January 2021 to Jun 2021, 48 modules were

**5** **Conclusion**

Light yield and attenuation length measurements were conducted for thirty-four non-S-type and one

S-type of 1.8 mm diameter Kuraray Y11 WLS fiber using a fiber scanner designed for the Mu2e

CRV detector. The fibers were purchased to enhance the light yield in the CRV’s critical sectors. A

significant light yield increase of about 25% was observed for the 1.8 mm over the 1.4 mm diameter

fibers. Preliminary measurements report less than 5% fiber aging per year and suggests negligible

aging effects for fibers more than five years old.

**3. Description of measurement apparatus**

The tiles used for our measurements are rectangular, with dimensions 3 _._ 4 _×_
3 _._ 4 _×_ 0 _._ 3 cm [3] . Each tile has a spherical cap indentation, called a “dimple,” at
the center of one of the large faces, with a radius of 6.1 mm and a depth of
1.6 mm. These dimples house the SiPMs. Three different scintillator materials
are used: cast polyvinyl toluene (PVT) based EJ-208 from Eljen Technology, [1]

PVT-based BC-412 from Luxium Solutions [2] (formerly Saint-Gobain), and a
polystyrene (PS) based molded tile produced at Fermi National Accelerator
Laboratory [3] (FNAL). Some of the tiles were wrapped in a reflective coating,
either Tyvek [®] or ESR. All wrappings had holes aligned over the SiPM dimple.
One tile was wrapped in black optical paper, covered by aluminum tape.
For one of the ESR wrappings, four 2.2 mm diameter holes, each centered on an
edge, approximately 5 mm in from the edge, were added for improved gas access
to the tile. For another new ESR wrapping, razor blade slits, approximately
1.5 cm long, centered on each edge, were added, also to improve gas access.
Wrappings were fastened with a sticker and also with Kapton [®] tape. ESR
wrappings were shaped into a tight envelope around the tile, while the Tyvek [®]

wrappings were loose. Figure 1 [left] shows a typical tile without wrapping,
Fig. 1 [center] shows the hole in the ESR wrapping over the dimple, and Fig. 1

[right] shows the ESR closure on the face away from the dimple.
The SiPMs were the S14160-1315PS SiPM from Hamamatsu (HPK) [4], except
that the glass window was replaced by the manufacturer with epoxy for increased
radiation hardness. They have an active area of 1 _._ 4 _×_ 1 _._ 4 mm [2] .
The currents from the SiPM were converted to a DC voltage using the RC
circuit (38.3 kΩ, 1 _µ_ F) shown in Fig. 2. The signal was read across the resistor.
